value.rationale: Matching deletion is a natural structured erasure of a symmetry-rich tight frame, and canonical orthogonal analysis projection norms quantify worst-case coordinate amplification after re-tightening. The exact all-matching-size profile and dimension threshold n=10, together with a uniquely optimal two-erasure amplification despite a third deletion reducing it, give a nonroutine stability and geometric incidence phenomenon. No unproved general consequence or minimal-projection interpretation is asserted.
